intro_html: Kharcho is the soup Georgia built on walnuts. Ground walnuts thicken the broth into something closer to a stew, tomatoes and vinegar keep it sharp, and rice cooked right in the pot makes it a meal instead of a starter. Coriander, cloves, and dill do the rest. Each bowl carries 38 grams of protein and 562 calories for about $5.76 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $5.76 a bowl (at everyday cost). Walnuts are the one splurge line on this list, and they are not a garnish here. They are the thickener, the fat, and half the flavor.
shop_smart: Walnuts are cheapest in the baking aisle rather than the snack aisle, and cheapest of all around the holidays. Buy then and keep them in the freezer, where they will not go rancid.
Rice cooks directly in the soup and thickens it as it goes. That means no separate pot and no separate cost line for a base.
Dried dill stands in for fresh without complaint in a long simmer. A jar lasts a year and costs less than two bunches of the fresh stuff.
Chuck roast again. A long simmer wants connective tissue, and connective tissue is exactly what the cheap cuts have.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into small cubes and simmer them in salted water for about 75 minutes, skimming the foam, until tender. Keep the broth in the pot.
In a separate pan, cook the chopped onion in the vegetable oil until soft and just golden.
Grind the walnuts to a coarse paste. A food processor is easiest, but a bag and a rolling pin works.
Stir the onions, ground walnuts, and diced tomatoes into the beef pot along with the coriander, cloves, cayenne, and garam masala.
Add the rice and simmer gently 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is tender and the soup has thickened.
Stir in the minced garlic, the red wine vinegar, and the dried dill and cook 3 more minutes.
Kill the heat, fold in the chopped cilantro, and taste for salt. Kharcho should be tangy, so add vinegar before you add salt.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Ladle that weight into each of 14 containers, stirring between scoops because the walnuts and rice sink. Each bowl lands at 562 calories with 38 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Georgian walnut soup for about $5.76 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Georgian kharcho meal prep: beef simmered with ground walnuts, tomatoes, rice, and dill into a thick, tangy soup. 562 calories, 38g protein, about $5.76 per serving (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: kharcho, georgian beef soup, walnut soup, beef and rice soup, budget meal prep, caucasus recipes
steps: Simmer cubed chuck roast in salted water about 75 minutes until tender.
Cook the onion in oil until golden and grind the walnuts to a coarse paste.
Stir onions, walnuts, tomatoes, and spices into the beef pot.
Add the rice and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until thickened.
Finish with garlic, vinegar, dill, and cilantro, then portion into 14 containers.
